In this paper, we propose a novel black-box Isolation checker for Relational DBMSs ,IsoRel. The core idea of IsoRel is to add two auxiliary columns into each table and instrument SQL statements in an isolation-agnostic manner. By analyzing the execution history of the instrumented SQL statements, IsoRel can infer dependencies among transactions that involve relational data models and complex SQL operations. We further evaluate IsoRel on all the isolation levels that these relational DBMSs support. In total, IsoRel has revealed 325 isolation anomalies. From these anomalies, we identify 48 unique isolation anomalies. Among the 48 isolation anomalies, 12 anomalies cause lost update, 12 anomalies cause read-write skew, and 24 anomalies cause write skew. These isolation anomalies violate the isolation levels defined by Adya [ 16,17], and have been confirmed by the respective DBMS community.
mentions.context_after: This result demonstrates that IsoRel can effectively handle the intricacies of relational data models and complex SQL operations. Such advancements would mitigate the risks associated with isolation anomalies and enhance the reliability of relational DBMSs. analysis.summary: This work checks isolation levels in relational DBMSs directly, rather than through the key-value abstraction existing isolation checkers assume. Because those checkers model only read(key) and write(key,value), they cannot represent the SQL operations real workloads use: of 48 isolation anomalies the authors collect, existing checkers identify 2. The approach builds dependency graphs over relational operations and detects the cycles that indicate each anomaly class.
analysis.narrative: SQLancer appears only in the future-work discussion, as background on what else DBMS testing covers: the paper notes that SQLancer and its approaches -- PQS, TLP and NoREC -- detect logic bugs in SELECT statements, that QPG uses query plans to guide testing, and that QuDi, GQT and GRev carry equivalent-query ideas to graph systems. That is a survey of the adjacent literature rather than a relationship: the paper's own comparison is against isolation checkers, and the anomaly work it builds on is Emme and TxCheck.

uses_infrastructure.reasoning: No reuse is described; the paper implements dependency-graph construction over relational operations.

extends_technique.reasoning: Isolation-anomaly detection through dependency-graph cycles shares no mechanism with the SELECT-oriented oracles the paper cites.
